business: MUN Prep App (AI preparation workspace for Model UN delegates, India-first, ₹199/week or ₹299/month)
by_segment: Club head or coordinator buying for a group
by_behaviour: First conference, no idea what to expect
Taught by a school MUN coach
Reads reviews and asks seniors first
why_not: My coach gives us material I can check with him. If the AI says something wrong in an unmoderated caucus I am the one standing there.
I always check reviews before paying and I could not find anyone who used this. That is not proof it works, that is proof nobody is saying it does.
226000 a year is not a lot and it is my own money. I would panic-buy the night before, but I would rather phone a friend who has done it.
There is no free trial and I never pay full price for something I have not tested. I will wait for a discount.
Our school coach runs sessions and my parents already paid 2500 for the conference. I will ask him, not an app.
My school coach hands us templates and checks our papers. I do not need to pay for the same thing.
I do everything the night before and I reach for whatever is already open. Asking an app to do MUN specifically has never occurred to me.
A senior in my WhatsApp group sent me their whole folder of old papers. I have free material sitting right there.
I use ChatGPT every day and it is fine. I am not paying for a version of what I already have without seeing a difference.
At 11pm the night before I would pay anything, but you have to show me something first. 199 for a week I will only use once is not convincing either.
I already have ChatGPT and my coach has templates. Adding one more thing to pay for is friction I do not need this week.
why_yes: I have three conferences this season and the difference between a good brief and a thin one is the difference between speaking and sitting silent. 299 is nothing next to what I spend on travel.
I have come second twice. Anything that sharpens my opening speech is worth a month of pocket money and 299 is nothing.
I have never been in committee and I am honestly scared. Having a brief ready in my own committee's words is worth more than the money.
I run my school's club and I would spend 299 to test it for the whole team. If it works I want it for twenty people, not one.
